header.name: 16 raw bytes; not a magic signature
header.eventRows: From byte28, signed32 ID and signed32 PC, stride8. Stop at first PC0 regardless ID; first matching event ID wins. ID0 with nonzero PC is ordinary.
header.pcFileOffset: 16 + 2 * signed32 PC, computed wide for reader bounds
header.nativeLimits: No captured native file bound, maximum row count, allocation-size guard, or overlap guard. Offline bounds are extra reader policy.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: mode0: little-endian I32 bits; mode1: little-endian float32 bits; mode2/3: U16 byte/word offset selected by sub
instructionGroups.flow: Normal next. mode2/sub>3 pushes @ADR/0. mode3/sub>3 has NULL load; no normal continuation assumed. High sub bits are ignored for immediates.
Normal next for selectors0..3. Selector3 writes native scratch initialized from script; >3 passes NULL to store helper.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: U16 byte count, U16 destination offset; selector=sub
instructionGroups.flow: Normal next requires valid pointers. Selector3 uses retained native scratch, not fresh script address. >3 supplies NULL; zero-byte CRT behavior is outside normal valid-pointer contract.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: U16 byte offset from popped decoded address
instructionGroups.flow: Normal next subject to valid address. Mode/sub bits do not change width.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: Embedded sub=word>>6; zero means DWORD store, nonzero byte count
instructionGroups.flow: Normal next subject to valid addresses. Bits4/5 ignored.
mode0 valid sub0,2..11; mode1 valid1,2,5..11; all other combinations status5. Always pops operand and restores/pushes result before normal exit.
mode0 sub0..11 arithmetic/logic; sub>11 retains left operand after pop2/push1 and continues. mode1 valid0..4; mode1>4 or mode>=2 status5.
sub0 branch only;1/2 condition-dependent target and next;sub>2 status5 after operand read. Target=int32(PC+2+relative). Bits4/5 ignored.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: Signed16 relative offset; sub frame size in DWORDs
instructionGroups.flow: Call target=int32(PC+2+relative); conditional return continuationPC+2. Bits4/5 ignored; native frame-4 storesreturnPC and frame-8 stores sub, no minimum guard.
0=status1 with stored PC+1 (possible resume);1=status2 exit;2=dynamic return from VM stack, zero returnPC status3;3/5/6/7/8/9 continue;4 or>9 status5. Bits4/5 ignored.
Descriptor address=table[bank]+16*index. argc=flags&0xffff; flag0x40000000 returns operandVector[0]. Native continuation conditional on callback returning and preserving relevant VM state.

instructionGroups.operandEncoding: little-endian signed32 relative bit pattern; sub frame size inDWORDs
instructionGroups.flow: Call target=int32(PC+3+relative), conditional returncontinuationPC+3. No ushort wrap. Bits4/5 ignored.

cfgPolicy: Start at the first nonterminating row per eventID. Never search unvisited bytes for trap-like words.
Mark branch alternatives, call continuation, yield resume and native continuation separately.
Return has an unknown stack-dependent edge, not sequential fallthrough.
Reject or diagnose out-of-payload/header targets, truncated operands, overlapping interpretations and budget exhaustion.
A static path is conditional; it does not prove runtime reachability, callback behavior, pointer/tag validity, or motion-event provenance.
Stored opcodes/operands are shown; runtime compatibility corrections and self-modification may alter executed values/code.
prototypePolicyDifferences: The research prototype rejects any negative/out-of-body declared entryPC; product may retain that row with diagnostic and omit its edge.
Prototype uses64MiB/4096events; product limits are independent bounded user-interface policy.
Prototype exposes explicit null-target error/boundary markers that product normalizes as diagnostics/terminal absence.
